summary: Jake H. Davis is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a PhD at CUNY Graduate Center. He held visiting faculty posts at Brown and Barre Center.
Jakob Bucher worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a missionary with the Basel Mission and became superintendent of the Anglo-Vernacular High School in 1890.
Jakob H. Thiessen was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at Kiel University between 1875 and 1880 under the supervision of Richard Pischel.

Jakob Halfmann specializes in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He held the Chair of Comparative Philology at the University of Würzburg (2023–2025) and became a group leader at the Free University of Berlin in 2026.

Jakob Hausheer studied at Zurich under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler and Adolf Kaegi, and earned his Ph.D. at Halle-Wittenberg. In 1905, he was appointed ordinary Professor for Old Testament Studies and Oriental Languages at the University of Zurich.
Jakob Steiner studied at Heidelberg University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Beuth Hochschule für Technik Berlin (1825–1834) and Frederick William University Berlin (1834–1863).

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer studied at Oxford and Tübingen, where he was mentored by Richard von Garbe. He served as Professor of Indology at Marburg (1925–1927) and held a chair at Tübingen from 1927 to 1945.
Jakub Čejka is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. He completed an MA (1990–1998) and a BA (2018) at Charles University.

James A. Benn is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar educated at Cambridge, SOAS, and UCLA (under Robert E. Buswell Jr.). He has taught at McMaster University, where he became Professor of Religious Studies.

James A. Santucci is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. His career includes serving as Professor of Religion and Chair of Comparative Religion at California State University, Fullerton (attested 1998–2007).
James Adam was a scholar of philosophy who completed his studies at the University of Aberdeen (circa 1876–1880) and at Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge (circa 1880–1884).

James Alan Matisoff is a linguist who earned his AB at Harvard and his PhD at UC Berkeley. After teaching at Columbia (1966–1969), he served on the faculty at the University of California, Berkeley from 1970 to 2002.

James Atkinson was a scholar of Iranian and Indological studies who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He served in the Indian Medical Service and was appointed Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College in 1818.
James B. Apple specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD in 1996 at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of John D. Dunne.

James Bird was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who earned an M.A. from the University of Aberdeen. He served as an assistant surgeon in Bombay Presidency, secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, and vice-president of The Asiatic Society.

James Bissett Pratt was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under William James. He spent his career at Williams College, serving as Professor of Intellectual and Moral Philosophy from 1917 to 1943.

James Blumenthal was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He taught at Oregon State University and Maitripa College.
James Bradstreet Greenough was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard University (A.B. 1856). He served on the Harvard faculty as a Tutor of Latin from 1865 to 1873.

James Burgess, educated at Glasgow and Edinburgh, was an archaeologist and Indologist. He founded the Indian Antiquary and Epigraphia Indica, and served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1886 to 1889.

James Burnell Robinson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa (attested 1996).
